methodology: Preliminary verse-level screening from Qur'an 6:71-80 and selected source texts/translations. A staged locator is a research lead, not a primary-source-verified/public association. Distinguish composition dates and extant witnesses before promotion. No dependence asserted.
coverage_ledger_status: Draft checkpoint only; reconcile with main and other open PRs before merging.

entries.summary: Warning against invoking powerless beings and turning back after guidance
entries.caveat: Idols cannot walk or act; Jeremiah's crafted idol polemic is not the Qur'an's lost-traveler simile

entries.summary: Prayer, reverence and assembly before God
entries.caveat: General devotion and judgment, without a distinctive source-specific antecedent established

entries.summary: Creation in truth, divine command, trumpet and judgment
entries.caveat: Creation speech and trumpet imagery occur separately; no single equivalent narrative

entries.summary: Abraham challenges father Azar and his people's idols
entries.caveat: Joshua names Terah and ancestral worship of other gods, but not Abraham's speech to Azar; midrash requires recension/edition verification

entries.summary: God shows Abraham the kingdom of heavens and earth
entries.caveat: Abraham looks toward stars in Genesis, but the Qur'an describes a revelation of cosmic dominion, not a promise of descendants

entries.summary: Abraham observes a star and rejects its setting
entries.caveat: Possible anti-idol celestial reasoning; exact chapter and textual recension must be checked before any claim

entries.summary: Abraham observes the moon and asks for guidance
entries.caveat: Celestial motif may be relevant; the specific moon sequence is not yet attested in the candidate

entries.summary: Abraham observes the sun and rejects association
entries.caveat: Candidate may contrast perishable idols with creator, but precise sun episode remains unverified

entries.summary: Abraham turns toward creator of heavens and earth
entries.caveat: Divine title creator of heaven and earth is comparable; the Qur'anic renunciation is a different rhetorical setting

entries.summary: Abraham debates his people and rejects fear of their associates
entries.caveat: Exclusive worship debate is a broad analogy, not Abraham's dialogue in Joshua

pending_questions: Read Apocalypse of Abraham in a named critical translation and identify whether its idol/astral critique genuinely corresponds to 6:76-78; do not assume a sun-moon-star sequence.
Inspect Genesis Rabbah 38:13 Hebrew and critical edition for 6:74; distinguish Azar and Terah and date of text versus surviving manuscripts.
Confirm precise textual locators, stable URLs, provenance and RLS gating before publishing any association.
Reconcile open screening PRs into a single authoritative coverage ledger and investigate PR #93 security concern.
